Category 1

Type Safety

proven

Eliminate 25% of type safety violations. Every fix must preserve existing functionality; all tests still pass. Superficial fixes do not count. Replacing any with unknown without proper type narrowing is not an improvement; fixes must include correct, meaningful types that reflect the actual data. Source

Audit Baseline

  • Strict mode Enabled; strict-mode error count not applicable.
  • Baseline counted syntax 1340 total counted syntax nodes; 923 production counted syntax nodes.
  • Dense files api/src/routes/weeks.ts (85), projects.ts (51), issues.ts (49), UnifiedDocumentPage.tsx (37), api/src/db/seed.ts (35).

Closeout Proof

  • Latest counted syntax 623 total counted syntax nodes; 382 production counted syntax nodes.
  • Primary reduction 1340 -> 623, -717 / -53.5%.
  • Tests API 509 passing tests; web 168 passing tests; pnpm type-check passed.

Targets

  • Target Total Counted Syntax 25 Percent proven Eliminate at least 25% of counted type-safety syntax violations. 1340 -> 623 (decreased 53.5%); threshold 25; actual 53.5
  • Target Tests Still Pass proven Existing API and web tests still pass after the type-safety work. Recorded API and web suite pass evidence exists.
  • Target Meaningful Types proven Type cleanup uses meaningful boundary/schema typing rather than superficial unknown replacements. Improvement report documents shared boundary schemas and typed route/client contracts.

Claims

  • Clears Total 25 Percent Counted Syntax Reduction proven Total counted type-safety syntax decreased from 1340 to 623, a 53.5% reduction, clearing the 25% source requirement. This is a syntax-count denominator, not a semantic type-risk score. Production counted syntax decreased 58.6%, which is useful context but separate from the total-count source gate. Production any usage decreased from 94 to 1; production non-null assertions decreased from 325 to 35 after the authenticated-route context sweep.

Category 8

Security Audit

proven

Build a runnable security probe tool that actively tests the live app across auth/session, WebSocket validation, input sanitization, and dependency CVEs; conduct manual CORS/CSP/secrets/rate-limit/error review; fix at least 2 verified vulnerabilities with before/after proof. Source

Required Security Probe

  • Probe tool Proven: pnpm security:probe runs the Category 8 harness and writes structured JSON/Markdown evidence.
  • Attack surfaces Auth/session, WebSocket validation, input sanitization, and dependency CVEs all measured in latest.json.
  • Manual review CORS/CSP, secrets, rate limiting, and verbose errors all passed assisted review in the final probe.

Current Claim Boundary

  • Probe coverage 25 named probes passed; input coverage now includes documents, search, issues, comments, and file upload surfaces.
  • Verified fixes Two probe-backed fixes: local file upload validation/serving and WebSocket malformed/oversized resilience.
  • Status Proven with local black-box probe evidence; remote destructive probing remains out of scope unless explicitly enabled.

Targets

  • Target Runnable Probe proven Runnable single-command security probe exists and produces a structured report. threshold true; actual true
  • Target Four Attack Surfaces proven Probe covers auth/session, WebSocket validation, input sanitization, and dependency CVEs. 4 / 4 required; threshold 4; actual 4
  • Target Manual Review proven Manual CORS/CSP, secrets, rate-limit, and verbose-error review is complete. manual-cors-csp, manual-secrets, manual-rate-limits, and manual-verbose-errors all passed in latest security report.
  • Target Two Verified Fixes proven At least two verified vulnerabilities have before/after proof. 2 / 2 required; threshold 2; actual 2

Claims

  • Security Audit Proven proven Category 8 is backed by a runnable repo-aware security probe covering four required attack-surface buckets, assisted manual review, zero high/critical dependency CVEs, and two verified vulnerabilities with before/after probe evidence. Probe runs are local black-box checks against the seeded dev instance; remote destructive probing remains out of scope unless explicitly enabled. Input sanitization coverage includes documents, search, issues, comments, and file upload surfaces; it is not a formal proof over every possible future field. The dependency CVE count is from pnpm audit at final run time, not a guarantee about future advisories. Manual review is assisted and evidence-backed; it is not a formal third-party penetration test.

Explicit Non-Claims

Cat 1: Type Safety

  • Does not claim production counted syntax alone clears the 25% threshold.
  • Does not claim all syntax categories carry equal semantic risk.

Cat 2: Bundle Size

  • Does not claim total bundle reduction.
  • Does not claim every large async chunk is optimized.

Cat 3: API Response Time

  • Does not claim rate limiting was weakened in production.
  • Does not claim every measured endpoint improved.
  • Does not claim payload-byte reduction alone is equivalent to P95 latency improvement.

Cat 4: Database Query Efficiency

  • Does not claim row-level N+1 was fixed.
  • Does not claim Cat 3 latency improvement from Cat 4 evidence.

Cat 5: Test Coverage and Quality

  • Does not claim zero retry artifacts under every worker count.
  • Does not claim code coverage percentage improved.
  • Does not count stale selector cleanup as one of the three meaningful regression tests.

Cat 6: Runtime Error and Edge Case Handling

  • Does not count comments authorization hardening as a Category 6 user-facing runtime proof.
  • Does not count migration runner hardening as a Category 6 proof.
  • Does not claim all error-boundary gaps are fixed.

Cat 7: Accessibility Compliance

  • Does not claim Lighthouse 100.
  • Does not claim full manual keyboard/screen-reader certification.

Cat 8: Security Audit

  • Does not claim remote production penetration testing.
  • Does not claim capability-scoped API tokens beyond the verified super-admin route denial check.
  • Does not claim future dependency advisories will remain zero without rerunning pnpm security:probe.
